references.text: The Psalms' expression of wanting to do God's will and having His law in the heart emphasizes the same principle as John 7:17: that the willingness to obey is the prerequisite for understanding and knowing God's truth.

The suffering servant describes how God opens his ear to listen, so that he can follow God's will; this example of attentiveness leads to knowledge of God's way, just as Jesus' promise that the willingness to do God's will leads to insight into His teaching.

In the same Gospel, Jesus confirms that whoever loves Him and keeps His word will be loved by the Father, and that He will reveal Himself to them; this is a direct parallel to the promise that the willingness to do God's will gives knowledge of the origin of the teaching.

Here it states that whoever is from God hears God's words, while those who are not do not hear. This is the reverse logic of John 7:17: the ability to know the truth (to hear) depends on one's willingness and belonging to God.
